title: Do the two ways of finding the shaded area really agree?
description: A big square holds four equal rectangles and a shaded square in the middle. Two children find the shaded area in two ways, one as the big square take away four rectangles and one as a square on the gap, and the video multiplies both out to match them. Keeko doubts the square of a take away, and a test with real numbers breaks the doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: to show two expressions are equal, multiply both out and match them part by part. Watch for students who write n minus m, all squared, as n squared minus m squared and lose the middle part.

source: Show that Tadang's expression (m + n)² − 4mn and Yusuf's exp
video_script.why: The child has two different-looking expressions for one shaded area and learns that multiplying both out is how to show they are equal.
video_script.substitution: Multiply out the big square minus four rectangles, multiply out the square on the gap, and compare the parts.
video_script.anchor: the big square of side m plus n holding four equal rectangles of sides m and n and a shaded square of side n minus m in the middle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko squares each part of n minus m separately and drops the middle part, so n minus m all squared becomes n squared minus m squared; with m as two and n as five this gives twenty one, not nine.
video_script.payoff_line: The two methods agree, and the shaded area is m squared minus two m n plus n squared

final_answer.spoken: m plus n all squared take away four m n equals n minus m all squared, which is m squared minus two m n plus n squared

names.Ruhee: finds the shaded square's area as the big square minus four rectangles
names.Ziva: finds the shaded square's area directly as a square of side n minus m

never_show: n² − m² as the square of n − m, marked as right
maths_rules: the big square has side m + n, so its area is (m + n)²
each of the four rectangles has area m × n, so together 4mn
the shaded area by the first method is (m + n)² − 4mn
(m + n)(m + n) = m × m + m × n + n × m + n × n = m² + 2mn + n²
the shaded square has side n − m, so its area is (n − m)²
(n − m)(n − m) = n × n − n × m − m × n + m × m = n² − 2mn + m²
slip: with m = 2 and n = 5, (5 − 2)² = 9 but 5² − 2² = 25 − 4 = 21
video_script.design: One idea: to show two expressions equal, multiply both out and match the parts. Wrong idea: the square of a take away is the take away of two squares. The big square figure stays all video; the working board holds the algebra.

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Second, multiply out the first area. Multiply m plus n by itself.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>That is m times m, plus m times n, plus n times m, plus n times n.
<bookmark mark='join'/>The two middle parts join, giving m squared plus two m n plus n squared.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Take away four m n. Two m n take away four m n leaves minus two m n.
<bookmark mark='area'/>The area is m squared minus two m n plus n squared.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks n minus m, all squared, is n squared minus m squared.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Try m as two and n as five. The shaded side is three, so its area is nine.

<bookmark mark='mid'/>A squared bracket with a take away needs its middle part, minus two m n.
